# AI Passport

> Open specifications for AI agents and other AI assets: a signed AI Passport that carries an asset's business context (who answers for it, where it sits in the organisation, who built it, its risk classification and purpose), and a revocation check, one HTTP call that any gateway or policy engine can enforce. Unable to ask means deny. Open draft 1.0-draft.1, with a conformance suite.

Start with section 1 of each specification. Instructions for coding agents are in AGENTS.md.

## Specifications

- [AI Passport v1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ServiceNow/ai-passport/main/spec/passport-v1.md): the signed document, its bindings and business context, and how a verifier checks it
- [AI Passport Revocation Check v1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ServiceNow/ai-passport/main/spec/revocation-check-v1.md): `GET /revocation?subject=…`, and what each answer means

## Implementing

- [Instructions for coding agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ServiceNow/ai-passport/main/AGENTS.md): what to read first, commands, and the rules implementations get wrong
- [Gateway example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ServiceNow/ai-passport/main/conformance/examples/gateway_check.py): the core of a gateway's check in about 50 lines
- [Conformance suite](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ServiceNow/ai-passport/main/conformance/README.md): how to run the test vectors against an implementation through an adapter

## Background

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ServiceNow/ai-passport/main/README.md): the problem, how it works, and who is behind it
- [FAQ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ServiceNow/ai-passport/main/FAQ.md): how AI Passport relates to JWT, OAuth, SPIFFE, Verifiable Credentials, status lists, CAEP and policy engines
